problem: The answer says the extra ΣLiLj product makes the denominator polynomial 'gain a wrong constant term'. That is true only when both loop gains are pure numbers. In an s-domain graph the loop gains are functions of s, so the product L1L2 adds a term that changes several coefficients (and possibly the degree) of the denominator, not just its constant.
fix: An extra product term L1L2, positive here because both loop gains are negative, is added to Δ. The denominator polynomial gains an extra term 6/((s+1)(s+2)) — in general a function of s, not a constant — so several of its coefficients change. The poles shift, and the predicted response no longer matches the hardware.
